--- title: "[markdown_to_html()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Parse CommonMark/GFM and render as HTML. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/multimark/blob/main/src/multimark/_cmark.py#L78-L232){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python markdown_to_html( text, *, hardbreaks=False, smart=False, normalize=False, sourcepos=False, unsafe=False, footnotes=False, extensions=(), options=0 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Takes a Markdown string and returns the corresponding HTML output. By default, raw HTML embedded in the Markdown is stripped for security (replaced with an HTML comment). Set `unsafe=True` to allow raw HTML passthrough. The parser is fully [CommonMark spec](https://spec.commonmark.org/) compliant. When GFM extensions are enabled via `extensions=`, additional syntax is recognized (tables, strikethrough, autolinks, tag filtering, and task lists). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [text]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Markdown string to parse and render. Can be any length, from a single inline fragment to a full document. Must be a Python `str` (not bytes). [hardbreaks]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Render soft line breaks (single newlines within a paragraph) as `
` tags. By default, this is `False` and soft breaks are rendered as spaces, matching the CommonMark specification behavior. [smart]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convert straight quotes to curly quotes, `--` to en-dashes, `---` to em-dashes, and `...` to ellipses. By default, this is `False`. [normalize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Consolidate adjacent text nodes in the parsed AST before rendering. This can produce slightly cleaner output in edge cases. By default, this is `False`. [sourcepos]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Include `data-sourcepos` attributes on block-level HTML elements indicating their line/column positions in the original Markdown source. Useful for building editors or source-mapping tools. By default, this is `False`. [unsafe]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Allow raw HTML and potentially dangerous links to pass through to the output without sanitization. When `False` (the default), raw HTML blocks and inline HTML are replaced with a comment ``, and dangerous URLs (e.g., `javascript:`) are suppressed. [footnotes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Enable footnote syntax parsing. When `True`, `[^label]` markers and `[^label]: content` definitions are recognized and rendered as numbered footnotes with backlinks. By default, this is `False`. [extensions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [()
]{.doc-parameter-default} : A sequence of GFM extension names to enable during parsing. Valid names are `"table"`, `"strikethrough"`, `"autolink"`, `"tagfilter"`, and `"tasklist"`. An empty sequence (the default) parses standard CommonMark only. [options]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : An integer bitmask of `Options` flags. Build it by OR-ing flags together, e.g., `Options.SMART | Options.UNSAFE`. This value is combined (via OR) with any named boolean parameters that are set to `True`, so you can mix both styles freely. Defaults to `0` (no additional flags beyond those set by keyword arguments). ::: ## Keyword Arguments Vs. Options Flags {.doc-keyword-arguments-vs-options-flags} The boolean keyword arguments (`smart`, `unsafe`, `hardbreaks`, etc.) are convenience shortcuts for the most common `Options` flags. Using `smart=True` is equivalent to passing `options=Options.SMART`. When both are provided, they are merged: `markdown_to_html(text, smart=True, options=Options.UNSAFE)` is the same as `options=Options.SMART | Options.UNSAFE`. Some flags (like `Options.GITHUB_PRE_LANG`, `Options.STRIKETHROUGH_DOUBLE_TILDE`, and `Options.LIBERAL_HTML_TAG`) have no keyword shortcut and can only be set via the `options` parameter. ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The rendered HTML string. Block-level elements end with a trailing newline. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Render basic Markdown to HTML: ::: {#b8b75ace .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import markdown_to_html markdown_to_html("**bold** and *italic*") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '

bold and italic

\n' ``` ::: ::: Enable smart punctuation: ::: {#2f9dd094 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_html('"Hello" -- world...', smart=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` '

“Hello” – world…

\n' ``` ::: ::: Allow raw HTML passthrough: ::: {#51c52fb6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_html("
custom
", unsafe=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` '
custom
\n' ``` ::: ::: Use GFM table extension: ::: {#0580635c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_html( "| A | B |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n", extensions=["table"], ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` '\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n
AB
12
\n' ``` ::: ::: Combine multiple features: ::: {#f130ac5e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_html( "~~old~~ -> new\n\nVisit https://example.com\n", extensions=["strikethrough", "autolink"], smart=True, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` '

old -> new

\n

Visit https://example.com

\n' ``` ::: :::
